note: Frozen: part of the eval subset, never fed to training. Probes anchored in the Phaedo's own scene and arguments (the prison death-day, the cyclical argument, the attunement objection) to separate it from the other four Platonic dialogues.

queries.query: Socrates' final request in the prison, after the poison began to work, that Crito repay a debt of a rooster owed to Asclepius
queries.note: The death scene's last words; 'cock', 'he was beginning to grow cold about the groin', 'his eyes were set' paraphrased away; 'Crito' and 'Asclepius' kept as names any reader of the scene knows.

queries.query: Socrates arguing on his last day that since opposites arise from opposites, the living must come back from the dead, so souls exist in the underworld awaiting return to birth
queries.note: The cyclical argument; 'go from this into the other world, and return hither', 'the complement of nature', 'revival' paraphrased away.

queries.query: Simmias' worry that the soul might be like the attunement of a stringed instrument, gone when the frame breaks, and Socrates' reply that the soul rules and opposes the body as no attunement could
queries.note: The harmony-and-lyre objection and its refutation; 'harmony', 'lyre', 'tensions and relaxations and vibrations of the strings' paraphrased away ('attunement of a stringed instrument' instead); 'Simmias' kept as a speaker's name.

queries.query: how are souls judged for their deeds after death, and can punishment cleanse them
queries.note: The closing myth's sorting of souls and the year in Tartarus for pardonable crimes; post-mortem judgment and purgation are pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: why must someone seeking truth withdraw from the senses and from bodily pleasures
queries.note: Purification as the soul gathering herself apart from the body; ascetic detachment as a condition of insight is answered by many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
